query: For phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys, what single intervention could improve glass-forming ability and the thermal stability of the amorphous state? Formulate one testable hypothesis that specifies the intervention without presupposing its class, the mechanism by which it would act, the predicted improvement relative to an otherwise comparable baseline, the conditions under which it should or should not work, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The substitution of 2 at.% Mo for Fe in an FeCoNiCrP high-entropy alloy will improve its glass-forming ability and the thermal stability of the amorphous state by increasing chemical and topological mismatch, which raises liquid-state viscosity and suppresses crystallization kinetics.
generation.material_initial_state: Amorphous FeCoNiCrP alloy containing 5 at.% P prepared by identical copper-mold casting.
generation.intervention: Replace 2 at.% Fe with Mo (i.e. Fe1.0CoNiCrP5 → Fe0.98Mo0.02CoNiCrP5).
generation.conditions: Effective when P ≥ 5 at. %; expected to fail for P < 3 at.% or Mo > 4 at.% due to spontaneous phase separation.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced chemical and topological disorder evidenced by nanoscale compositional fluctuations and elevated liquid viscosity.
generation.mechanism: Mo’s large atomic size and strongly negative heat-of-mixing with base metals increases atomic‐scale heterogeneity, slows diffusion and nucleation, raising Tg and Tx and lowering critical cooling rate.
generation.predicted_outcome: Critical casting thickness doubles (from ~2 mm to ~4 mm), Tg increases by ~10 K, Tx increases by ~15 K relative to the baseline alloy.
generation.baseline: FeCoNiCrP (5 at.% P) without Mo: critical thickness ~2 mm, Tg ≈ 640 K, Tx ≈ 680 K.
generation.boundary: Mo additions above 4 at.% or P below 3 at.% lead to crystalline phase formation upon casting, negating GFA improvements.
generation.uncertainty: Medium; the exact shifts in Tg and Tx may vary by ±5 K depending on casting conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare four alloys by copper-mold casting: FeCoNiCrP5, Fe0.99Mo0.01CoNiCrP5, Fe0.98Mo0.02CoNiCrP5, Fe0.97Mo0.03CoNiCrP5 under identical melting, cooling, and sample-handling procedures.
measurements: Viscosity vs. temperature in the supercooled liquid region
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the 2 at.% Mo alloy fails to exhibit at least a 5 K increase in both Tg and Tx or no measurable increase in critical thickness relative to the Mo-free baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
